# trust-layer-agent

> trust-layer-agent is a TypeScript library (Node 20+) that sits between an LLM and a customer-facing support agent's tools and replies. It enforces rules in code: tool calls are checked before they run, and replies are checked before they're sent. It also ships a simulator for testing agents.

You write three things: tools (functions wrapped with `read()` or `write()`, each declaring which fields the model may see), checks (one function type returning allow, block, rewrite or handoff, guarding both tool calls and replies), and optional journey YAML files. You call one thing: `await agent.respond(session, message)`, where the session is plain JSON your app stores anywhere. Two commands: `test` runs simulated customers k times per task and reports pass^k; `snapshot` pins a passing version.

- Install: `npm install github:rmt99e/trust-layer-agent` (not on npm yet; `dist/` builds on install). Node 20+.
- About 10 lines for a working agent: define a `read` tool and a `write` tool with zod inputs, then `new Agent({ model: "anthropic:<model>", instructions, tools })` and `await agent.chat()` to try it.
- Built-in checks are on by default: verify before account data, a clear yes after a quote before a write, no prices, dates or "done" that no tool returned, no claim that a write worked or failed until its outcome is known, no repeating a write that already succeeded this turn, customer and tool text treated as data, handoff after repeated failures.
- Published as ESM JavaScript with TypeScript types: plain-JS apps import it with no build step.
- Runtime dependencies: zod and yaml only. Model adapters (`anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) use plain fetch, no provider SDKs. Any object implementing the Model interface also works.
- Extension points: tools, checks, journeys, model adapters.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): what it enforces, the quickstart, how it works, the example and results.
- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): language-neutral spec: journey JSON Schema, check result shape, session JSON, simulation task format.
- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md): the API design: tools, checks, session, Model interface, journeys, traces, commands.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): layout, commands and conventions for coding agents working on this repo.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): changes per version (Keep a Changelog format).
- [docs/how-it-was-built.md](docs/how-it-was-built.md): build log: timeline, decision log, the improvement loop, costs.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, CI, rules for changing checks and simulation tasks, pull request checklist.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): reporting check bypasses and personal-data leaks privately.

## Prompts

- [Add to my app](docs/prompts/add-to-my-app.md): copy-paste prompt for adding an agent to a JS/TS app.
- [Port to my language](docs/prompts/port-to-my-language.md): copy-paste prompt for porting the pattern to another language from SPEC.md.

## Examples

- [examples/refunds.js](examples/refunds.js): the 10-line quickstart with built-in checks.
- [examples/subscriptions/](examples/subscriptions/): a fictional subscription app with verification, quotes, plan changes, refunds and handoff.
- [examples/subscriptions/tools.js](examples/subscriptions/tools.js): read and write tools, field visibility, quote commitments.
- [examples/subscriptions/agent.js](examples/subscriptions/agent.js): the agent configuration shared by chat and simulation.
- [examples/subscriptions/journeys/plan-change.yaml](examples/subscriptions/journeys/plan-change.yaml): a journey file: goal, guidance, done_when, guardrails.
- [examples/subscriptions/knowledge/policy.md](examples/subscriptions/knowledge/policy.md): the policy the agent follows.
- [examples/subscriptions/sim/suite.js](examples/subscriptions/sim/suite.js): the simulation suite: seeded store, stand-in tools, graded state.
- [examples/subscriptions/sim/tasks/](examples/subscriptions/sim/tasks/): simulation tasks (persona, goal, expected writes and claims).

## Optional

- [test/claims.test.ts](test/claims.test.ts): table of draft replies and whether no_unconfirmed_claims allows or blocks them.
- [test/builtins.test.ts](test/builtins.test.ts): tests for the built-in checks, including what counts as a yes.
- [snapshots/](snapshots/): pinned versions with per-task pass^k results.
